title: Flightctl RPC operations v2
description: SUPERSEDES rpc-ops-v1 (all v1 ops keep their names; chat-load/chat-unload become aliases of endpoint-load/unload for one release). Every operator/UI action addresses records by PUBLIC id (G25); holders authenticate token operations with principal + token; the server derives identity from the socket peer (+ optional bearer token) and IGNORES any identity in the request. x-ops is the normative authorisation/MCP/CLI table: 'role' is checked first, then the token 'scope', then policy.approval_matrix for 'approval'. MCP tools are generated 1:1 from rows with mcp=true and carry no extra privilege.

admission.description: v2 admission: identity is NEVER supplied by the caller (v1 'ingress' removed). Dormant federation hooks (delegation, signed_manifest) are not accepted in v2 requests at all: the closed object rejects them (fail closed).

shadow_of.description: Set only by the legacy shim in tee mode: the request mirrors a legacy lanes.sh call whose outcome is given. The authority decides as if live, executes nothing, and records shadow-decision/shadow-divergence events.

ttl_s.description: Rolling expiry from grant; renew extends it. Not the ceiling.

max_s.description: Optional requested ceiling; the authority uses min(max_s, lane, quota, class ceilings). A request above the quota limit is 403 quota_exceeded naming the limit, never silently clamped.

lease_ref.description: Holder addressing: the token alone (legacy form; the authority looks up the lease) or the public lease_id plus the token. Both require the authenticated principal to own the lease.

approve_args.description: v2 drops the caller-supplied 'evidence' object of v1: touch/PIN evidence is derived only by the server's verifier.

wait_s.description: Long-poll: return as soon as an event >= since_seq commits, or after wait_s with an empty page.

evidence_seq.description: seq of an event carrying a fresh executor inspect (status ok, no tenants, cgroup empty or absent) taken AFTER the quarantine; the authority re-inspects and refuses if it no longer holds.

session_open_args.description: Amendment 3 rev 2 (Sol 6.1 amd3 P1-4): key_fingerprint names one of the caller's enrolled, unrevoked keys (session-key-enrol); the authority resolves it to the key bytes (resolve_session_key) only after the friend gates admit the request, and sends the bytes over the executor wire; an unknown, revoked or foreign fingerprint is 'not_found'.

session_key_enrol_args.description: Amendment 3 rev 2: enrol one public key for the CALLER's own principal (account-scoped; the principal comes from the peer, never from args). Refused with 'unavailable' while features.friend_sessions is off; 'conflict' if another principal holds the same unrevoked key. Rev 3: a revoked fingerprint is refused with 'conflict' until the operator purges it (session-key-revoke purge).

session_key_revoke_args.description: Amendment 3 rev 2/3: revoke one of the caller's keys (the operator: anyone's). Works while friend sessions are off (it removes friend state). A revoked key never resolves and is never re-enrolled, by anyone: its record stays as a tombstone (rev 3, Sol 6.1 amd3r2) until the OPERATOR purges it (purge=true, an already revoked key; 'denied' for anyone else), after which it may be enrolled again as a new record. Open sessions keyed by a revoked key are closed by the authority (session-close).

x-ops: - (may return 202 waking: an explicit fetch may wake the lane host)
